action: UTA students, employees and event-form users: watch for a university notice, be alert to messages using your details, and avoid sharing sensitive data through campus web forms until it is confirmed safe.
date_note: Date is when The Record and UTA's FAQ reported the incident; UTA says it was first discovered on 26 October 2026.
exec: A university took a web-form portal offline after personal data was accessed, a reminder to inventory and limit what online forms collect.
plain: The University of Texas at Arlington says someone got into its systems and accessed personal information. The university has not said whose data or how many people are affected.
summary: UTA says a cybersecurity incident first discovered on 26 October 2026 let someone access personal information; it is working with law enforcement and outside experts and has no list of affected people yet. The MachForms portal for event registration, service requests and surveys was taken offline. The Record reports the Qilin ransomware gang claimed the attack that week; UTA names no actor.
title: University of Texas at Arlington says personal information was accessed in a cyber incident

validation.note: UTA's own FAQ read; The Record adds the portal and the Qilin claim. UTA says 'accessed', The Record says 'stolen'. Number affected not stated.

review.note: Compared title, 26 Oct discovery, personal information accessed, MachForms offline, law enforcement and experts, no affected list against UTA FAQ (13 Nov) and The Record (13 Nov); Qilin claim attributed to The Record only, UTA names no actor
